messages:
sam: hey @alex — quick one, CI started failing because our Basic auth header in requests is showing extra double quotes when pulled from .env on Windows. logs show: \"\"Basic YmFzZTY0...\"\" :facepalm:

alex: ugh, PowerShell/SetX behavior. People accidentally include quotes when setting env vars. If you run `setx REDWOOD_API_KEY 'abc'` the literal quotes get written. Use either no quotes or the .NET setter: 
```powershell
setx REDWOOD_API_KEY abc
# or for current user without the extra wrapping quotes
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('REDWOOD_API_KEY','abc','User')
```

sam: ah nice — that was the exact mistake. Also noticed our Node app does `Authorization: \"Basic ${b64}\"` in logs (the extra escaped quotes came from a faulty header concat). For reference, this is the recommended Node pattern: 
```js
// Node example (no SDK)
const apiKey = (process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || '').trim();
const b64 = Buffer.from(`${apiKey}:`).toString('base64'); // trailing colon => empty password
const res = await fetch(url, {
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Basic ${b64}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
});
```

maria: small note — our JS SDK (redwood-client) accepts { apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY } in the constructor and will set the header for you. Prefer that over manual header construction where possible (avoids small mistakes).

jordan: in browsers use `btoa(apiKey + ':')` instead of Buffer; watch out for unicode in keys (rare).

sam: how about curl/debugging? I used both forms during debugging: 
```bash
# using curl's -u (adds trailing colon for empty password)
curl -u "$REDWOOD_API_KEY:" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/endpoint

# or explicit header (portable across shells):
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"$REDWOOD_API_KEY:\" | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/endpoint
```

alex: also watch dotenv and CRLF/BOM issues on Windows — a BOM or stray \r can get into the value and break base64. Quick local checks: `node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY))"` or `python -c 'import os,sys;print(repr(os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY")))'`. If you see quotes or \r, strip them with `.trim()` or `.strip()`.

ci-bot: FYI: GitHub Actions secrets are injected without quotes, but YAML can be tricky. Don't wrap secrets in single quotes under `env:` if you don't want literal quotes. Example: 
```yaml
env:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }} # good
  # BAD: REDWOOD_API_KEY: '\${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}' # will include quotes literally
```

sam: perfect — fixed the setx entry and trimmed in code, CI green now. thanks! :tada:

alex: one last tip — Basic auth requires the trailing colon after the username (api key) to represent empty password. Forgetting the colon will change the decoded auth and fail.

sam: noted. closing this out.
